change: No structural changes. Confirmed: Lats (Latissimus Dorsi) and biceps (Biceps Brachii) as co-primaries are correct per EMG research (PMC5548150) showing high lat and bicep activation in suspension chin-ups. Secondary mid back (Rhomboids + Lower Traps), Lats (Rotator Cuff), forearms (Wrist Flexors) and abs are appropriate. Removed Wrist Extensors from forearms consideration as grip on chin-up is primarily flexor-dominant. Original had only Wrist Flexors so no change needed.

Fixed: merged the two separate 'mid back' entries into one. The original had 'mid back' (Rhomboids) in primary and 'mid back' (Upper Traps, Lower Traps) in secondary, violating the rule that a bucket must appear in only ONE entry. Merged all three latins (Rhomboids, Upper Traps, Lower Traps) into a single primary 'mid back' entry alongside Posterior Deltoid. Removed the redundant secondary mid back entry. Biceps Brachii retained as secondary.

Fixed: abs secondary entry had only 'Upper Rectus Abdominis'; added 'LowerRectus Abdominis' to reflect full core bracing during leaned-back suspension front raise. Both heads of rectus abdominis are engaged isometrically during this exercise. No other changes.

Fixed: forearms secondary changed from [Wrist Flexors, Wrist Extensors] to [Wrist Flexors] only. Grip during hanging is a flexor-dominant action; wrist extensors are not meaningfully activated. Hip flexors (iliopsoas) are biomechanically a significant mover in leg raises but have no allowed bucket in the schema; omitted per rules. Note: hip flexor engagement is not representable in current schema.

Fixed: forearms secondary changed from [Wrist Flexors, Wrist Extensors] to [Wrist Flexors] only. Same reasoning as bent-leg version — grip is flexor-dominant. Straight-leg version additionally loads Rectus Femoris (Quads) as a hip flexion assist, but note this is already somewhat captured via the straight-leg movement pattern. Quads could be added as secondary (Rectus Femoris assists hip flexion in straight-leg raise), but given the primary framing is abs-focused and no other version lists quads, leaving consistent. Hip flexors (iliopsoas) not representable in schema — flagged.
